label: Rick Owens
basis: Written from published runway and lookbook imagery and the house's own colour names (black, dust, bone, milk, natural). It is a claim about how that work would MEASURE on these four descriptors, not a measurement of it: no Owens image was passed through influence/descriptors.py, because none is in this corpus. No one with expertise in the work has checked these numbers. Treat every field here as a hypothesis with a name attached, and see docs/influence/README.md on what an authored pack may and may not be used to argue.

palette.note: Near-monochrome and dark: a large black mass, a charcoal, a dust grey, and a bone highlight, with almost no chroma anywhere. The corpus mean for the largest cluster is L*=66.7 (paper) against L*=10 here, so this is the field the pack actually asserts. The fractions say the dark is not just present but dominant - one mass over half the frame rather than six even regions. chromaMean 1.5 against a corpus mean of 7.8 is the strongest single claim in the file.

form.note: Soft-edged and vertical. Hardness is pulled out of the top bin (corpus mean 0.341, the corpus's own largest) and into bins 1-3, because drape resolves over many pixels where a printed rule resolves over two. Orientation is raised on bins 5 and 6 together, not bin 6 alone: the synthetic probes put a vertical stroke at the 5/6 boundary, so an authored spike on 6 alone would be claiming a precision the descriptor does not have. curvatureMean below the corpus reads as long continuous curves rather than many small turns; elongation above it reads as a columnar silhouette. straightFraction is deliberately NOT authored - it is 0.001 +/- 0.011 across all 19,807 works, so any value written there produces an enormous z off a dimension that is nearly constant, and the pack would push hardest on the one number the corpus cannot distinguish.
